test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: general
question: A tap can fill a tank in 5(1)/(2) hours. Because of a leak, it took 8(1)/(4) hours to fill the tank. In how much time (in hours) will the leak alone empty 30% of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of filling (Tap A) = 1 ÷ (11/2) = 2/11 units/hr

Rate with leak (Tap A + Leak L) = 1 ÷ (33/4) = 4/33 units/hr

Rate of leak (L) = 2/11 − 4/33 = (6 − 4)/33 = 2/33 units/hr

Time for leak to empty 30% = (30/100) ÷ (2/33) = 0.3 × (33/2)

Time = 9.9/2 = 99/20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 99/20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Time taken by Tap A = 5 1/2 hours = 11/2 hours

Time taken by Tap A and Leak L together = 8 1/4 hours = 33/4 hours

Let Total Work (Capacity) be the LCM of numerators (11, 33) = 33 units

 
 

 **Person / Pipe**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency (units/hr)**
 
 

 Tap (A)
 11/2
 33 units
 33 ÷ (11/2) = 6
 
 

 Tap + Leak (A + L)
 33/4
 33 ÷ (33/4) = 4
 
 

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of Tap (A) = 6 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of Tap + Leak (A + L) = 4 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of Leak (L) = Efficiency (A + L) − Efficiency (A)

⇒ Efficiency of Leak (L) = 4 − 6 = −2 units/hr (Negative sign denotes emptying)

⇒ Total work to be done by Leak = 30% of Total Capacity

⇒ Work = 30% × 33 = 0.3 × 33 = 9.9 units

⇒ Time taken by Leak = Work ÷ |Efficiency of Leak|

⇒ Time = 9.9 ÷ 2

⇒ Time = 99/20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 99/20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Work Concept

In Pipes and Cisterns, an inlet pipe does positive work while a leak or outlet pipe does negative work. Total efficiency = Inlet efficiency − Outlet efficiency.

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Time is inversely proportional to Efficiency for a constant amount of work. Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency.

LCM of Fractions

To find the LCM of fractions like a/b and c/d, use the formula: LCM (a, c) ÷ HCF (b, d).</p
